requirements.summary: An instruction gets a place and a free physical register; it is refused when the buffer is full or no register is free.
A completion is taken once, for an instruction in the buffer; any other completion changes nothing.
A flush cancels every younger instruction and restores the mapping, also when two instructions write the same logical register.
The completed head retires in order with its value; an allocation in the same cycle sees the room before the retirement.
An instruction with an exception is not retired: it and every younger instruction are cancelled and the committed state stays.
The committed value of every logical register is the one of sequential execution, also after a reset with instructions in flight.
